question: Do DAFRC/market DAF contribution and account totals include sweepstakes and charity-auction gross receipts at Pledgeling Foundation, Our Change Foundation and Charities Aid Foundation America (2022-23), as at Givinga? Quantify the correction per year from Schedule G Part I line 2b (gross, retained) against Schedule D Part I and the DAFRC panel, and decide whether Pledgeling's 20-23k 'accounts' are platform-user records
conclusion_affected: DAF contribution totals; account counts; processor share
rationale: Schedule G screen found three more sponsors where online sweepstakes/auction agents collect 41-85% of gross receipts booked as contributions (CAF America Omaze $105.6m in 2022; Pledgeling $36.8-38.9m; Our Change $14.7m in 2025). All data is in filed XML, so the correction is scriptable

question: Can pool asset weights for Vanguard Charitable, DAFgiving360 and NPT be recovered from public fund documents (mutual-fund SAI 'control persons and principal holders' tables, N-PORT, annual reports listing the sponsor as a 5%+ holder) so their in-fund cost per DAF dollar can be asset-weighted as Fidelity's (26.3 bps) was?
conclusion_affected: All-in cost per DAF dollar, nationals vs community foundations
rationale: Only Fidelity publishes pool balances (audit Note 3). The others leave bounds of 1-59, 3-67 and 7-61 bps. Fund SAIs name record holders above 5% with share counts, which would pin down the largest pools

question: Screen all parsed 990s for sponsors whose Part VIII line 3 investment income is under 50 bps of average total assets (MS GIFT: 4-35 bps vs 128-424 bps at 11 nationals) as a filing-level marker of account-level fees netted against income; check each hit's Schedule D Part XII line 4a and circular fee terms
conclusion_affected: How far Part IX understates donor-borne cost at broker and wealth captives
rationale: MS GIFT's wrap fees are invisible in Part IX and in Part XI/XII. The only filing-level trace found is an order-of-magnitude-low line 3 yield. A universe screen would show whether other broker captives share the pattern
